findings.title: Unbounded memory allocation in AMQP binary deserialization
findings.impact: Denial of Service: attacker can send AMQP message with oversized length-prefix to cause OutOfMemoryError, crashing the client or server.
findings.evidence: readBytes() allocates byte[contentLength] where contentLength is read from untrusted AMQP wire protocol (line 86). The check at line 87 allows allocation up to Integer.MAX_VALUE - 1 bytes (~2.1 GB). Called recursively from readLongstr(), readTable(), readArray() via readFieldValue().

findings.title: Unbounded recursion depth in AMQP field value deserialization
findings.impact: Denial of Service: attacker can cause StackOverflowError by crafting deeply nested AMQP table or array structures, crashing the client.
findings.evidence: readFieldValue() is recursive. Case 'F' (line 181) calls readTable(), which calls readFieldValue() in a while loop (line 150). Case 'A' (line 184) calls readArray(), which calls readFieldValue() in a while loop (line 245). No recursion depth counter or maximum nesting level enforced. Attack vector: send nested table structure Table{Table{Table{...}}} 10,000+ levels deep.

defects_to_look_for.mechanism: A length field read from untrusted input decides the size of a buffer, and that buffer is created before the corresponding payload has been shown to exist.
Decoding routines call one another in a cycle with nothing counting how deep the cycle has gone, so nesting in the input controls the depth.
